column1: # The level 1 swipe corpus (bead tla-7xql.4, epic tla-7xql).
# 48 items in one template, the pilot described in swipe/level1/TEMPLATES.tsv.
# Every item pins a STATE and asks a question about it, so unlike level 0 it
# shows a model screen. swipe/level1/render.sh builds that screen and
# swipe/level1/bake.sh measures the verdict.
# Rows are tab-delimited and carry the literal marker ITEM in field 1, so
# prose in this file can never be read as data. Read rows with awk -F'\t' or
# cut, never with IFS=$'\t' read: tab is IFS whitespace, so a run of tabs
# collapses and an empty field vanishes.
# AN ITEM ROW. Thirteen fields, in order. Fields 1 to 11 keep their level 0
# meanings so harness/swipe/stemblind.sh reads this table with --items and no
# code change, and 12 and 13 are what a pinned rung adds:
#    1  marker      the literal ITEM
#    2  id          L1-<template>-<nn>, stable, never renumbered
#    3  template    E1, resolving to a TEMPLATES.tsv row
#    4  ask         the tag shown WITH the question: enabled, terminal or
#                   implies. It names which of the epic's question kinds the
#                   line is and it does NOT determine the answer
#    5  kind        the item's own kind: true, false, vacuous, illformed,
#                   wronglevel or unparsed. The reader never sees it
#    6  swipe       right, left or down. Derived from field 5 by the bake
#    7  rc          the exit code of the INVARIANT run. Written by the bake
#    8  pin_states  how many states the pin admits. AUTHORED and then
#                   confirmed by the bake's postcondition. A - means 1
#    9  claim       the single line the reader answers
#   10  vacuity     a level 1 witness that the claim is vacuous, or -
#   11  flash       the one line shown after the swipe, always present. On a
#                   false, vacuous, illformed, wronglevel or unparsed item it
#                   is the correction. On a true item it is the reason the
#                   claim holds, because there is nothing to correct about a
#                   true statement. Frank ruled on 2026-10-18
#   12  model       the reading/ module the item is about
#   13  pin         the pinned state, written as a TLA+ conjunction. The bake
#                   uses it verbatim as Ini and render.sh splits it on /\
#   awk -F'\t' '$1 == "ITEM" && $12 == "Brackets"' swipe/level1/ITEMS.tsv
#   grep '^ITEM' swipe/level1/ITEMS.tsv | cut -f5,12 | sort | uniq -c
# FIELDS 6 AND 7 ARE OWNED BY swipe/level1/bake.sh. Do not hand-edit them.
# Field 5 is the author's PREDICTION and the bake is there to contradict it.
# Over this corpus it contradicted six of the forty-eight.
# THERE IS NO SECOND EXIT CODE HERE, and that is the first thing a level 0
# reader will look for. Level 0 stores a PAIR because ASSUME exits 10 both
# when the claim is false and when it fails to evaluate, so one number cannot
# split them. The level 1 INVARIANT channel is already five-valued: 0 holds,
# 12 false, 75 does not evaluate, 76 is not a state predicate at all, 150 does
# not parse. One number says which.
# ROW 76 IS THE ONE THIS TEMPLATE EXISTS FOR. TLC's message is "The invariant
# Claim is not a state predicate (one with no primes or temporal operators)",
# and a reader who writes Pop where they mean ENABLED Pop has asked whether a
# STEP holds at a STATE. The bead's own words are that people conflate "the
# guard is true" with "the action can fire"; this is that conflation one layer
# further out, and TLC names it exactly. The kind is called wronglevel.
# THE PIN MUST SATISFY THE MODEL'S OWN TYPE INVARIANT AND NEED NOT BE
# REACHABLE. Nothing in the mechanization constrains a pin: a pin of open = 5
# violates Brackets' own Surplus invariant and ENABLED Pop still reads rc 0,
# because the generated .cfg names Claim and nothing else. TypeOK is the
# model's own statement of what a well-formed state is and it costs one TLC
# run. Reachability costs a model check and would cut the item space hard, and
# ENABLED is a question about a state rather than about a history. CENTRAL
# TOOK THIS RULE AND FRANK HAS NOT RULED ON IT.
# FIELD 8 IS A HAZARD AND NOT BOOKKEEPING. Ini is a predicate rather than an
# assignment, so it may admit more than one state, and then INVARIANT Claim
# asks whether the claim holds at EVERY state it admits. Measured:
# text = <<>> /\ open \in 0..1 with ENABLED Pop reads 12, because the claim
# splits across the two states. Four items here pin three states on purpose,
# because Handover's CONSTANT Site = {s1, s2, s3} is a set of MODEL VALUES and
# a model value is not an identifier the pin module can name. Measured:
# Ini == holder = s1 comes back rc 150 with a semantic error on s1, so
# holder \in Site is the only pin Handover has. The bake confirms the count
# with a POSTCONDITION, so a pin that admits more states than its author
# thought reddens rather than shipping a different question.
# ITEMS ARE AUTHORED IN MATCHED GROUPS, which is what keeps the stem-blind
# gate green. The unit is either a four, one item of each of four kinds built
# from one idea, or a pair, a true and a false built from one idea. Six fours
# and twelve pairs is 48, and it lands the mix at 18 true, 18 false and 12
# down without anybody counting. Rows sit in their authoring groups so a
# reviewer sees a matched pair side by side, and ids are never renumbered.
# THE SWIPE MIX IS LEVEL 0'S AND THE KIND MIX IS NOT. Right is 18 of 48, so
# the base rate is 0.3750 and the power table in swipe/README.md transfers
# unchanged. That argument is about the SWIPE mix, which is why it carries.
# The kind mix under down does not: level 0 splits 12 into 6 vacuous, 5
# illformed and 1 unparsed over five kinds, and this rung splits it 4 vacuous,
# 3 illformed, 3 wronglevel and 2 unparsed over six.
# A CLAIM MAY ONLY NAME A DEFINITION THE SCREEN SHOWS. Decision D7 withholds
# Init, Next and Spec, so a terminal item asks ~ENABLED (Push \/ Pop) and
# never ~ENABLED Next: a reader cannot evaluate a name they have not been
# given. swipe/level1/render.sh --list-shown is the authority and
# harness/test-swipe-enabled.sh asserts it over every row.
# NO ITEM MAY DEPEND ON \div WITH A NEGATIVE DIVIDEND. TLC 2026.07.31.184830
# breaks the contract its own Naturals.tla states. The note in
# swipe/level0/ITEMS.tsv carries the measurement and bead tla-7n7e is open on
# it. No claim or pin here uses \div at all.
# FIELD 11 IS NOT OPTIONAL. L2 on the epic: a falsehood is reproduced later at
# .19 with no feedback, .15 with a bare verdict and .04 with the verdict plus
# the correction. The gate rejects a blank one and a stub.
ITEM
column11: The open count is 1, so Pop's first conjunct holds, and the text is shorter than Limit, so its second one does too.

column1: ITEM
column11: The antecedent holds at a text of length 1, and Pop still cannot fire, because open is 0 and Pop needs it above 0.

column1: ITEM
column11: The text has length 3, so the antecedent is false and the line says nothing about Pop at all.

column1: ITEM
column11: Pop is an action and the line asks whether it holds at one state. Write ENABLED Pop to ask whether it can fire.

column1: ITEM
column11: Push asks only that the text be shorter than Limit, and an empty text is.

column1: ITEM
column11: Pop needs open above 0 and nothing has been pushed yet, so there is no open bracket to close.

column1: ITEM
column11: Pop is disabled, so the second arm is evaluated, and Head has no value on an empty sequence. The line does not denote.

column1: ITEM
column11: ENABLED binds looser than = here, so SANY refuses the line. Write (ENABLED Pop) = TRUE, or drop the comparison.

column1: ITEM
column11: Both of Pop's conjuncts hold: open is 5 and the text has room for one more bracket.

column1: ITEM
column11: The open count is 6 and that is only Pop's first conjunct. The text is already at Limit, so the second one fails and Pop cannot fire.

column1: ITEM
column11: Both actions need the text shorter than Limit and it is exactly Limit, so neither can fire and the run stops here.

column1: ITEM
column11: A state is terminal only when every action is disabled. Push is enabled here, because the text has room.

column1: ITEM
column11: PollTake asks only that nobody holds the lock, which is what the antecedent says, so the consequent follows.

column1: ITEM
column11: Nobody holds the lock, so the antecedent holds, and TaskTake also asks that the task not have been served yet. It has.

column1: ITEM
column11: The task holds the lock here rather than the poller, so the antecedent is false and the line says nothing about TaskDrop.

column1: ITEM
column11: PollTake is an action, so the line asks whether a step holds at a state. Write ENABLED PollTake.

column1: ITEM
column11: Nobody holds the lock and the task has not been served, which is both of TaskTake's guard conjuncts.

column1: ITEM
column11: Nobody holds the lock, which is the conjunct that is easy to stop at. The task has already been served, so the second conjunct fails.

column1: ITEM
column11: PollDrop asks that the poller hold the lock, and it does.

column1: ITEM
column11: PollTake asks that nobody hold the lock. The poller holds it, so taking it again is not a step this model has.

column1: ITEM
column11: Nobody has asked for a break and neither player is playing, so Start holds for either one of them.

column1: ITEM
column11: A break has been asked for, and Start's first conjunct rules it out for every player at once, so no witness exists.

column1: ITEM
column11: Nobody is playing, so the set the quantifier ranges over is empty and the line holds without Stop being looked at.

column1: ITEM
column11: Player is {p1, p2}, so playing has no value at "q" and Stop's guard does not denote. ENABLED does not rescue it.

column1: ITEM
column11: A break has been asked for and nobody is playing, which is both of Resume's conjuncts.

column1: ITEM
column11: A break has been asked for, so the first conjunct holds, and both players are still playing, so AllIdle is false.

column1: ITEM
column11: Nobody is playing, so the antecedent holds, and Ask needs only that no break has been asked for yet.

column1: ITEM
column11: Nobody is playing, so the antecedent holds. Ask cannot fire, because a break has already been asked for and Ask needs the opposite.

column1: ITEM
column11: Stop asks only that the player be playing, and both of them are.

column1: ITEM
column11: Neither player is playing, so Stop's guard fails for both and the universal has a counterexample.

column1: ITEM
column11: The holder wants to hand over, and Site has three members, so there is always another site to hand to.

column1: ITEM
column11: Grant's first conjunct is want, and nobody wants to hand over here, so the existential below it is never reached.

column1: ITEM
column11: Nobody wants to hand over, so the antecedent holds, and that is exactly Request's own guard.

column1: ITEM
column11: Somebody wants to hand over, so the antecedent holds, and Request asks for the opposite, so it cannot fire.

column1: ITEM
column11: Eliminate asks that the ring hold more than one place, and this one holds two.

column1: ITEM
column11: One place is left in the ring and Eliminate needs more than one, so nobody can be counted out.

column1: ITEM
column11: Eliminate is enabled, so the second conjunct is evaluated, and the ring holds two places rather than three. The line does not denote.

column1: ITEM
column11: A prime cannot sit on the operand of ENABLED, and SANY refuses the line rather than picking a reading. ENABLED is already about the next step.

column1: ITEM
column11: Eliminate is the only action, and one place left in the ring disables it, so the counting is over.

column1: ITEM
column11: Three places are left, so Eliminate can still fire and the state is not where the counting stops.

column1: ITEM
column11: Every heap is empty, so each of Take's three arms quantifies over 1..0, which is empty, and no arm has a witness.

column1: ITEM
column11: Two heaps are empty and the third holds 2, so Take's third arm has a witness and the game is not over.

column1: ITEM
column11: Take is an action and a state cannot satisfy one. Write ENABLED Take to ask whether a move is left.

column1: ITEM
column11: The first heap is empty, so the antecedent is false and the line holds whatever Take can do.

column1: ITEM
column11: MoveA carries no guard at all, and it is still enabled only when 1..b has a member to move a to. Here b is 5.

column1: ITEM
column11: MoveA is enabled here, so its negation is false. An action with no guard is not an action that never fires.

column1: ITEM
column11: Each action leaves the other's variable alone, so together they ask that a sit in 1..b and b sit in a..N, and both do.

column1: ITEM
column11: Neither action has a guard and both can fire from here, so this is as far from terminal as the model gets.
